key_insight: Microscopic residual impurities in wide-bandgap perovskite films act as degradation nucleation sites, and they can be rapidly detected with microscopy plus machine learning before devices fail.
engineering_relevance: This enables fast, non-invasive pre-screening of perovskite films to flag stability risk early, supporting scalable manufacturing of more durable solar cells.
method: Nano-FTIR to chemically identify impurity compositions
High-resolution reflected-light microscopy to image impurity distributions
Machine learning-assisted image analysis for seconds-level impurity detection
evidence_signal: Photo-stress and degradation-tracking experiments showed that higher impurity density correlates with faster early degradation and that failure starts at impurity–perovskite interfaces.
watch_item: The diagnostic framework is chemically validated for the studied film system, but transfer to other perovskite compositions and manufacturing conditions will need re-calibration.
paper_title: High-Throughput Imaging of Degradation-Inducing Microscopic Impurities in Perovskite Solar Cells
